title: Full-output cavity phase error prices intrinsic loss, cooperativity and linewidth separately
statement: In the declared one-photon Markov cavity model r(delta)=1-kappa/[i*delta+(kappa+lambda)/2+g^2/(i*delta+gamma/2)], complete-output unitarity gives error_sigma^2=2*(1-sigma*Re(r)). Empty on-resonance minus branch has error^2=4*lambda/(kappa+lambda). On-resonance plus branch at lambda=0 has error^2=4/(1+C),C=4*g^2/(kappa*gamma). body: The wanted reflected amplitude and every unwanted output form a unit vector, so comparison to sigma times the free reference gives the exact squared error2*(1-sigma*Re(r)), not a reflection-conditioned fidelity. For error<=eta, the empty-center branch needs lambda/(kappa+lambda)<=eta^2/4; the zero-intrinsic coupled branch needs C>=4/eta^2-1. A strictly smaller target uses strict inequalities. At eta=.01 these thresholds are2.5e-5 and39999 in the respective branches. In the empty, lossless detuned branch error^2=16*delta^2/(kappa^2+4*delta^2), so a halfband Delta requires kappa>=2*Delta*sqrt(4/eta^2-1); Delta=.05B,eta=.01 gives about20B. kappa is the useful linewidth, lambda intrinsic loss; the C formula here assumes lambda=0. No assertion combines independently saturated branch limits into sufficient full-band operation. Physical dispersion, positive-frequency completion, photon handling and actual hardware costs remain unresolved.
